text: Hallelujah! Praise the LORD from the heavens; praise him in the heights.
Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his hosts.
Praise him, sun and moon; praise him, all you shining stars.
Praise him, highest heavens, and you waters above the heavens.
Let them praise the name of the LORD, for he commanded and they were created.
He set them in place forever and ever; he gave a decree that will never pass away.
Praise the LORD from the earth, you sea creatures and all ocean depths,
fire and hail, snow and mist, stormy wind that obeys his word,
mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars,
wild animals and all cattle, creeping things and birds on the wing,
kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all judges of the earth,

versions.text: kings of the earth and all nations, princes and all rulers of the earth,
versions.explanation: שֹׁפְטֵי means 'judges' (those who govern and render justice), a distinct term from the 'kings' and 'princes' already named; 'rulers' loses that nuance and duplicates the sense of the earlier terms. Also לְאֻמִּים is better rendered 'peoples' than 'nations' here, keeping the human-groups sense parallel with the leaders listed.

text: young men and maidens alike, old men and children together.

versions.text: young men and women alike, old and young together.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew distinguishes four groups: בחורים (young men), בתולות (maidens/young women), זקנים (old men/elders), and נערים (boys/children). The current rendering uses 'young' twice in one short line, which blurs the four-fold list and creates an awkward echo when read aloud.

text: Let them praise the name of the LORD, for his name alone is exalted; his splendor is above earth and heaven.
He has raised up a horn for his people, praise for all his faithful ones, for the children of Israel, the people close to him. Hallelujah!
